tool.name: Cyclospora Mt-Junction caller
tool.description: anchor-and-count repeat-length calls for the 8th CDC marker, from reads
tool.version_command: python3 -c "import sys; print('cyclospora junction caller @TOOL_VERSION@ (python %s)' % sys.version.split()[0])"
tool.command:
## ------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Galaxy runs the container with --contain --cleanenv --no-mount tmp, ## so /tmp inside is the image's own read-only one and TMPDIR arrives ## empty. Point scratch at the job directory, which IS bind-mounted. ## ------------------------------------------------------------------ mkdir -p wrk && export TMPDIR="\$(pwd)/wrk" &&
## ------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Specimen id. An explicit name wins; otherwise take the element ## identifier of the reads, which is what a collection element carries. ## Keep only characters that are safe in a shell word and in a sheet ## column, so no quoting hazard can reach the command line. ## ------------------------------------------------------------------ #set $raw = str($specimen_name).strip() #if not $raw #if $reads.reads_source == 'bam' #set $raw = str($reads.bam_input.element_identifier) #elif $reads.reads_source == 'fastq_collection' #set $raw = str($reads.fastq_collection.element_identifier) #else #set $raw = str($reads.fastq1.element_identifier) #end if #end if #set $spec = "".join([c for c in $raw if c.isalnum() or c in "._-"]) #if not $spec #set $spec = "specimen" #end if
## ------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Stage inputs under real names. Galaxy datasets are extensionless ## .dat files; the caller decides gzip vs plain text from the suffix. ## ------------------------------------------------------------------ #if $reads.reads_source == 'bam' ln -s '$reads.bam_input' 'reads.bam' && #elif $reads.reads_source == 'fastq_collection' ln -s '$reads.fastq_collection.forward' 'reads_R1.${reads.fastq_collection.forward.ext}' && ln -s '$reads.fastq_collection.reverse' 'reads_R2.${reads.fastq_collection.reverse.ext}' && #else ln -s '$reads.fastq1' 'reads_R1.${reads.fastq1.ext}' && ln -s '$reads.fastq2' 'reads_R2.${reads.fastq2.ext}' && #end if
python3 '$__tool_directory__/junction_caller.py' --specimen '$spec' #if $reference.ref_source == 'history' --junction-ref '$reference.junction_ref' #else --junction-ref '$__tool_directory__/refs/junction.fa' #end if #if $reads.reads_source == 'bam' --bam 'reads.bam' #elif $reads.reads_source == 'fastq_collection' --fastq 'reads_R1.${reads.fastq_collection.forward.ext}' 'reads_R2.${reads.fastq_collection.reverse.ext}' #else --fastq 'reads_R1.${reads.fastq1.ext}' 'reads_R2.${reads.fastq2.ext}' #end if --min-reads $min_reads --min-freq $min_freq $emit_specimen_column #if $emit_diag --diag '$diag' #end if --out '$junction'

param.name: reads_source
param.label: Reads to scan
param.help: READS, not the marker-aligned BAM. The junction locus is not a contig in markers.fa, so a filtered marker BAM contains no junction reads at all and yields NO_CALL / marker_absent with flank_reads=0 for every specimen. That failure looks exactly like a clean negative.
param.option: BAM of unaligned reads (uBAM, or the unmapped fraction)

param.name: bam_input
param.label: BAM of reads
param.help: An unaligned BAM, or the unmapped fraction of a mapping run. Alignment information is never used; every primary record's sequence is scanned in both orientations. Do NOT pass the marker-aligned, MAPQ-filtered BAM.

param.name: specimen_name
param.label: Specimen id
param.help: Leave blank to use the element identifier of the reads. Characters outside A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ - are dropped.

param.name: ref_source
param.label: Junction reference set
param.help: The bundled file is CDC's MAPPING_JUNCTION_WITH_PRIMERS_FEB_2020 set, 20 records, shipped with the tool. Override only to track a newer CDC release.

param.name: junction_ref
param.label: Junction reference FASTA
param.help: Records must share one constant LEFT flank; the shortest record is taken as the zero-repeat class, i.e. LEFT+RIGHT.

param.name: min_reads
param.label: Minimum spanning fragments for a call
param.help: PRE-REGISTERED at 3. Not a relaxed gate: Tn5 cuts inside the AT-rich repeat array, so typical spanning depth is 2 to 15 fragments even at ~900k reads while thousands of reads carry only one flank.

param.name: min_freq
param.label: Minimum fraction of spanning fragments
param.help: PRE-REGISTERED at 0.05. Mixed infections are real: every array passing both gates is emitted.

param.name: emit_specimen_column
param.label: Prepend a specimen column
param.help: Keep this ON for Galaxy. A Galaxy dataset is called dataset_N.dat, so the sheet builder cannot recover the specimen id from the file name. Turn it OFF only to reproduce the reference implementation's output byte for byte.

param.name: emit_diag
param.label: Also write the diagnostics JSON
param.help: Read counters: reads_scanned, left_anchored, left_anchor_only, right_anchor_only, spanning_reads, spanning_fragments, discordant_fragments, flank_reads. This is how a true negative is told apart from the wrong input file.

tool.help:
**Cyclospora Mt-Junction caller** — repeat-length genotypes at the 8th CDC marker, by anchor-and-count over raw reads.
The Mt-Junction locus is a tandem array of a 15 nt motif between two constant flanks:
``` [ LEFT 64 nt constant ][ array = n x 15 nt ][ RIGHT 45 nt constant ] ```
A read is **spanning** if it contains the 18 nt left anchor (the last 18 nt of LEFT, ending exactly at the array start) and, after it, the 18 nt right anchor. Reads matching only the reverse complement of the left anchor are reverse complemented first. What lies between is the array; its length must be a multiple of 15 and it must be N-free. Both mates of a fragment cover the same short insert, so arrays are collapsed per fragment and mates that disagree are discarded as discordant. There is **no assembler** anywhere in this: only 3 to 15 fragments span the array even in a deep run.
-----
**Give it reads, not the marker BAM**
The junction locus is *not a contig in* `markers.fa`, so junction reads never reach the marker-aligned, MAPQ-filtered BAM. Feeding that BAM here is not an error that announces itself; it silently returns `NO_CALL … marker_absent` with `flank_reads=0` for every specimen. Measured on `C_IA031_18`:
| input | reads scanned | flank_reads | call | |---|---|---|---| | trimmed FASTQ pair | 384,530 | 1,294 | `Mt_Cmt199.A_Junction_Hap_17`, 8 fragments | | uBAM of the same reads | 384,530 | 1,294 | identical | | `C_IA031_18.filtered.bam` | 52,048 | **0** | `NO_CALL / marker_absent` |
Accepted: trimmed FASTQ (two datasets or a paired collection), an unaligned BAM, or the unmapped fraction of a mapping run.
-----
**Gates — pre-registered, do not tune**
* `--min-reads 3` spanning **fragments** * `--min-freq 0.05` of the spanning fragments
The low fragment floor is a property of the library prep, not a loosened threshold: the array is extremely AT-rich, Tn5 prefers exactly that, so tagmentation cuts *inside* the array and most fragments stop there. Thousands of reads carry one flank while a handful span. That is also why CDC has no junction call for 50 of the 153 benchmark specimens.
-----
**Output**
One tabular file, always written, one row per passing array (plus a `specimen` column when that option is on):
`length_class`, `matched_reference`, `reads`, `freq`, `repeat_count`, `ref_seq_length`, `motifs_all_known`, `closest_reference`, `closest_mismatches`, `flag`, `total_spanning_reads`, `flank_reads`, `sequence`.
`reads` counts spanning **fragments**. An array with no exact reference is reported as `NOVEL` with its length class — never dropped, never snapped to the nearest reference. When nothing passes, one `NO_CALL` row is written and `flag` says which kind of nothing it was:
| flag | meaning | |---|---| | `marker_absent` | no read carried either flank; suspect the wrong input file | | `marker_present_but_no_spanning_fragment` | flanks seen, array never spanned | | `below_threshold` | spanning fragments seen, none passed the gates |
Optional diagnostics JSON carries the counters behind that distinction.
-----
**Two caveats the caller keeps honouring**
1. `Mt_Cmt127.A_Junction_Hap_2` is **135 bp on disk, not 127** — a truncated right flank plus 11 nt of Nextera adapter. The `Cmt<length>` in a name is a length class, never a key; the caller keys off repeat count and array sequence only, and holds the right anchor at 18 nt so Hap_2 still matches. 2. CDC's 2022 nomenclature contains classes absent from the Feb-2020 20-reference set (`Cmt139` = 2 repeats, `Cmt229` = 8), so any repeat count is permitted.
-----
Ported from `a1_junction.py` of the LoFreq/PyEuk Cyclospora typing arm. Against CDC's own calls on the 153-specimen benchmark: precision 1.000, recall 0.971, zero disagreements.
